subject: Latency safety nets & traffic spike runbook

Subject: Latency safety nets & traffic spike runbook

Alex / Priya — thanks for the call earlier. Quick written recap so we have a single place to iterate on the runbook and next steps. TL;DR: we captured target SLOs, fallback rules, and an initial joint test plan (attached). Please confirm items marked ACTION and any corrections.

Summary of agreed items:
- SLO targets
  - Normal steady-state: P95 generation latency <= 300 ms (single-token latency averaged across streaming shards).
  - Controlled spike mode: P95 <= 600 ms for sustained traffic up to 3k concurrent requests; absolute latency should not exceed 1.2s for any single request.
- Concurrency & throughput
  - Target sustained concurrency: 1,200 concurrent sessions.
  - Burst capacity target: absorb instantaneous full-fan-in to 3,000 concurrent sessions with graceful degradation.
- Autoscaling behavior
  - Warm pool: maintain a configurable warm pool of ready capacity; initial proposal: 20% of committed baseline kept warm during known business hours.
  - Scale-up time: target median scale-up to meet 80% of observed spike load within 90 seconds; 95th percentile under 150 seconds.
  - Fast-path: pre-warmed fast-path instances to serve <150 ms p50 where possible.
- Queueing and safety-net behaviors
  - Overflow policy: token-aware queueing with max queue depth 500 requests; requests older than 45s should be rejected with a clear 429+retry-after header.
  - Graceful fallback: route to lower-cost, lower-latency model variant if latency crosses threshold for more than 30s.
- Streaming requirements
  - Chunk emission latency: first streaming chunk <= 50 ms after generation begins; progressive token emission with <25 ms inter-chunk variability preferred.

Action items (owners):
- Alex / SRE (ACTION): confirm target spike windows and any blackout windows for warm pool testing.
- Priya (ACTION): provide expected traffic shape PDF and retention/audit constraints (we need RPS histograms).
- Karthik (internal): finalize warm-pool sizing calc + telemetry hooks and attach to the test plan.
- Mina (internal): schedule a 2-hour joint test window and coordinate data capture.

Attached: priming-test-plan.pdf (test scenarios, scripts, expected telemetry), warm-pool-snapshot.xlsx (initial sizing worksheet).

If this reads correctly I’ll convert to a short mutual action plan and propose two dates for the joint test.

On Thu, Jun 10, 2027 at 10:12 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex / Priya — thanks for the call earlier. Quick written recap so we have a single place to iterate on the runbook and next steps.

Couple of technical notes and a suggested tweak to warm-pool behavior:
- Warm-pool sizing: rather than a flat 20% we should use a decayed-percent-by-hour model (20% during high-hours, 10% off-peak) and a short-term lookahead that primes extra instances when the expected 5-minute RPS derivative exceeds a threshold. I put the sizing calc in warm-pool-snapshot.xlsx (sheet: dynamic-model).
- Scale signals: use a combination of (a) queue depth, (b) observed p95 token latency, and (c) incoming connection ramp rate. Trigger pre-warm when 5-min derivative > 30% and queue depth > 50.
- Telemetry hooks: we will emit the following metrics to the SRE bucket: request_id, model_variant, shard_id, start_ts, first_chunk_ts, final_ts, returned_tokens. We can retain request-level logs for 30 days and push to an external S3 endpoint via a signed transfer (requires customer bucket policy).
- Test plan additions: add a scenario that toggles fallback to the low-latency model after 30s sustained breach; capture client-observed degradation (stream interruption, token gaps) and server reject codes.

I’ll upload a short workbook with the expected metric names and a sample Grafana dashboard link; Mina — can you add that to the attachments before we send to BrightMart?

- Karthik
